title: Smart Plant Watering Scheduler
description: An AI-powered plant management app using a Perceptron classifier and Simulated Annealing optimizer to predict watering needs and find optimal watering routes.
longDescription: Smart Plant Watering Scheduler is an interactive web application that combines machine learning and metaheuristic optimization to intelligently manage garden plant watering. Users register plants on a responsive visual garden grid with positional data, growth stage, and soil conditions. A custom-built Perceptron classifier — trained via cross-validated gradient descent — predicts whether each plant needs water. A Simulated Annealing engine then solves the watering route optimization problem, minimizing total Euclidean travel distance while penalizing skipped thirsty plants and unnecessary watering of healthy ones. The app features a frame-by-frame SVG animation overlaid on the garden map, a live Chart.js cost-evolution graph, and a full iteration log table — all rendered in real time.
challenges: Training a Perceptron classifier to generalize across varied plant conditions without overfitting
Designing a Simulated Annealing cost function that balances distance, missed waterings, and unnecessary treatments
Rendering a responsive garden grid where plant markers stay fully visible at any screen width
Animating the SA search frame-by-frame over an SVG path overlay synchronized with a live cost chart
solutions: Implemented k-fold cross-validation with an adaptive learning rate to tune the Perceptron and prevent overfitting
Crafted a multi-factor cost function with weighted penalties for skipped thirsty plants, excess waterings, and total Euclidean path length
Used percentage-based CSS positioning so plant markers pin responsively to the garden grid regardless of device width
Built a frame-buffer replay system that steps through SA iterations, redrawing SVG paths and pushing data points to Chart.js in real time

title: Distributed Book Catalog System
description: A microservices-based backend system for managing book inventory, search, and purchase operations with RESTful APIs.
longDescription: A distributed backend system designed using a microservices architecture to manage a book catalog and handle purchase operations. The system is composed of three independent services: an API gateway (frontend service), a catalog service for managing books and inventory, and an order service responsible for handling purchases. Services communicate via REST APIs and are containerized using Docker. The project demonstrates core distributed system concepts such as service separation, API gateway pattern, inter-service communication, and database interaction using SQLC with SQLite/Turso.
challenges: Designing a microservices architecture with clear service responsibilities and communication flow
Handling inter-service communication using synchronous HTTP calls
Managing data consistency during book purchase operations across multiple services
Implementing pagination and structured API responses
Ensuring reliable database access with type-safe queries
solutions: Separated the system into three services (API gateway, catalog, order) following single responsibility principles
Implemented RESTful communication between services with a centralized API gateway
Used SQLC to generate type-safe database queries and reduce runtime errors
Added pagination middleware to standardize list queries across endpoints
Containerized all services using Docker for easy deployment and environment consistency
